tracks.narration: Two charges in empty space — what does each one feel from the other?
Place a positive charge here and another positive charge there. The line between them is the line of force. Like signs push apart; opposite signs pull together.
The strength of that push or pull follows Coulomb's law: F equals k times q one q two divided by r squared. Three knobs — the two charges and the distance.
Watch what the inverse square does. As we slide the second charge away, the force does not just fall — it falls fast. Twice the distance, one quarter the force.
Same shape as Newton's gravity, but stronger by far — and signed. Charges can pull or push; mass only ever pulls.
